concepts.description_formal: For f continuous on [a,b], the average value of f over [a,b] is the definite integral of f over [a,b] divided by b minus a.
concepts.description_plain: The average value of a function is its accumulated amount divided by the length of the interval.
concepts.name: Average value of a function over an interval
concepts.notation: average value of f on [a,b]

concepts.description_formal: The average value of f on [a,b] has the units of f; the average rate of change of f on [a,b] is the difference quotient of f and has the units of f divided by the units of the input.
concepts.description_plain: Averaging a function is not the same as averaging its rate of change.
concepts.name: Average value contrasted with average rate of change
concepts.notation: average value; average rate of change

concepts.description_formal: For a particle in rectilinear motion, the definite integral of the velocity function over a time interval equals the displacement of the particle over that interval.
concepts.description_plain: Integrating velocity gives the net change in position, not the length of the trip.
concepts.name: Displacement as the definite integral of velocity
concepts.notation: displacement; net change in position

concepts.description_formal: For a particle in rectilinear motion, the definite integral of the absolute value of the velocity function over a time interval equals the total distance travelled over that interval.
concepts.description_plain: Integrating the absolute value of velocity gives how far the particle actually travelled.
concepts.name: Total distance as the definite integral of speed
concepts.notation: speed as the absolute value of velocity; total distance

concepts.description_formal: If s is an antiderivative of v then s(b) equals s(a) plus the definite integral of v over [a,b], and the same relation holds between v and a.
concepts.description_plain: A later value equals the starting value plus the accumulated change.
concepts.name: Position and velocity recovered from an initial value
concepts.notation: s(b) = s(a) + integral of v

concepts.description_formal: If Q has rate of change q on [a,t] then Q(t) equals Q(a) plus the definite integral of q from a to t.
concepts.description_plain: The amount now is the amount at the start plus everything accumulated since.
concepts.name: Amount at a time from an initial amount and a rate
concepts.notation: Q(t) = Q(a) + integral of q

concepts.description_formal: For a quantity with inflow rate f and outflow rate g, the net rate of change is f minus g and the net change over an interval is the definite integral of that difference.
concepts.description_plain: When something enters and leaves at once, the net rate is the difference of the two rates.
concepts.name: Net rate as rate in minus rate out
concepts.notation: rate in minus rate out

concepts.description_formal: The amount function attains its absolute maximum on a closed interval at a critical point where the net rate changes sign from positive to negative or at an endpoint, and a global argument is required to decide between the candidates.
concepts.description_plain: The stored amount is largest where the net rate changes from positive to negative, endpoints checked.
concepts.name: Extreme value of an accumulated amount from the sign of the net rate
concepts.notation: candidates test on an accumulation function

concepts.description_formal: A complete interpretation of a definite integral of a rate names the accumulated quantity, the interval of accumulation, and the units formed as the rate units times the input units.
concepts.description_plain: An integral of a rate names a quantity, over a stated interval, in stated units.
concepts.name: Meaning of a definite integral in context
concepts.notation: interpretation with units

concepts.description_formal: For f greater than or equal to g on [a,b], the area of the region bounded by the two graphs and the vertical lines x equal a and x equal b is the definite integral of f minus g over [a,b].
concepts.description_plain: The area is the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve across the interval.
concepts.name: Area between two curves integrated in x
concepts.notation: upper minus lower; dx

concepts.description_formal: The limits of an area integral are the inputs at which the boundary of the region changes, found by solving the equation of the two curves or read from the stated bounding lines.
concepts.description_plain: The limits come from where the curves meet or from the lines the region is bounded by.
concepts.name: Limits of integration from the boundary of the region
concepts.notation: intersection points as limits

concepts.description_formal: For curves written as functions of y with p greater than or equal to q on [c,d], the area of the region between them is the definite integral of p minus q with respect to y over [c,d].
concepts.description_plain: Slicing horizontally, the area is the integral of the right curve minus the left curve.
concepts.name: Area between two curves integrated in y
concepts.notation: right minus left; dy

concepts.description_formal: When two curves intersect at an interior point of the interval, the area is the sum of definite integrals over the subintervals, on each of which the order of subtraction is fixed.
concepts.description_plain: Where the curves swap places the region has to be cut and the pieces added.
concepts.name: Region split where the boundary curves cross
concepts.notation: sum of definite integrals; absolute value of a difference

concepts.description_formal: If a solid has cross sections perpendicular to an axis with area A at each input, its volume is the definite integral of A over the interval the solid spans.
concepts.description_plain: Add up the areas of the slices across the interval.
concepts.name: Volume as the integral of a cross sectional area
concepts.notation: volume as the integral of A

concepts.description_formal: For a solid built on a plane region, the side of a cross section at an input is the difference of the boundary functions at that input, measured in the direction perpendicular to the axis of slicing.
concepts.description_plain: The side of each slice is the distance between the two boundary curves.
concepts.name: Cross sectional dimension read from the region
concepts.notation: side length as a difference of functions

concepts.description_formal: The integrand for a solid with known cross sections is the area formula of the named shape evaluated at the distance between the boundary curves.
concepts.description_plain: Each named shape has its own area formula, applied to the same distance.
concepts.name: Cross sectional area from the shape of the slice
concepts.notation: area formulas for triangles and semicircles

concepts.description_formal: When a region bounded by a curve and the axis of revolution is revolved about that axis, the cross sections are discs of radius equal to the distance from the curve to the axis, and the volume is pi times the definite integral of the square of that radius.
concepts.description_plain: Revolving a region against the axis makes discs whose radius is the curve.
concepts.name: Disc method for a solid of revolution
concepts.notation: pi times the integral of the radius squared

concepts.description_formal: For revolution about the horizontal line y equal k, the radius at an input is the absolute difference between the function value and k, and correspondingly for a vertical line x equal h.
concepts.description_plain: When the axis moves, the radius becomes a difference from that line.
concepts.name: Radius measured from a line other than an axis
concepts.notation: radius as f minus k or k minus f

concepts.description_formal: For a region between two curves revolved about an axis it does not meet, the volume is pi times the definite integral of the square of the outer radius minus the square of the inner radius.
concepts.description_plain: When the region does not touch the axis the slices are rings with two radii.
concepts.name: Washer method for a region held away from the axis
concepts.notation: pi times the integral of outer squared minus inner squared

concepts.description_formal: For revolution about a horizontal or vertical line, the outer and inner radii are the distances from the far and near boundary curves to that line, and the volume is pi times the integral of the difference of their squares.
concepts.description_plain: Both radii become distances from the shifted line.
concepts.name: Washer radii measured from a line other than an axis
concepts.notation: outer and inner radii as shifted differences

concepts.description_formal: For f with continuous derivative on [a,b], the length of the graph of f over [a,b] is the definite integral of the square root of one plus the square of f prime with respect to x.
concepts.description_plain: The length of a graph is the integral of the square root of one plus the square of the slope.
concepts.name: Arc length of a curve given by a function
concepts.notation: arc length integral
